theme.title: Rotation: Growth → Value & Defensives
theme.summary: Health Care (+2.03%) and Consumer Staples (+1.31%) led the market today, while Technology (-2.53%) and Industrials (-1.47%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -1.65% versus +0.93% for defensives and -0.58% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained -0.32% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -1.64%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at -1.75%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX rose 6.94% to 16.33, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 2.07% to $4,098.70, crude oil was little changed at $95.39, and bitcoin slipped 1.91% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
